identity.name: load_coa_notices
identity.description: Reads a pinned, sha256-verified manifest of Toronto Committee of Adjustment Notice of Decision PDFs (2017 first), extracts each document's text IN MEMORY, parses every minor-variance item into one coa_notice_variances row, and stores VALUES ONLY - no PDF, no notice text, no names (Spec 129 §D3). A class-A guarded upsert with soft retire (retract departed_mark) in one step-scoped transaction, behind pre_write checks that refuse to write or retire from a bad parse or an incomplete acquisition. McBylaw Phase 2 oracle C.

why_lock.text: Mutual exclusion with every other writer of coa_notice_variances (Spec 47 §A.5 lock registry row 129; Spec 129's own number, globally unused). The lock is declared here and acquired by the library from descriptor.identity.lock; scripts/load-coa-notices.js keeps `ADVISORY_LOCK_ID = 129` as a §5.4 source-text constant, asserted equal by src/tests/steps/load_coa_notices/violations.test.ts C-2. It holds across acquisition, parse, write and score, because a second concurrent run would fetch the same documents twice and race the soft retire.

why.text: Spec 129 §D9. Class A guarded upsert keyed on variance_key: a re-run over the same pinned manifest and extractor writes zero rows. The guard covers every VALUE column and excludes the version stamps (extractor_version, vocab_version), loaded_at and retired_at, so a version bump rewrites only rows whose values changed. SOFT RETIRE (retract departed_mark): a key the reconciled parse no longer yields is MARKED retired_at = now() and UNMARKED when it reappears, in the same transaction, behind the library's empty-set and mass-retire guards (coa_notices_retire_max_pct). No oracle row is ever deleted; consumers read retired_at IS NULL. The MARK is table-wide (scope none), which is why the values-only batch family (aic_values_batch, Spec 129 §2b) is a second acquisition form of this ONE primary and not a second step: one run sees both families, so neither retires the other.

Spec 129 §2c (operator CHAT-74.IN4): the plan facts of the pinned values batches are written as a derived second target of this one primary, inside its transaction (Spec 124 R-DY). The prior-state read is the required derive form and is unused: the rows are DATA the reconcile hands to deriveRows (RE-FREEZE #40), emitted once with slice 0.

Spec 129 §2c. Class A guarded upsert keyed on application_number: a re-run over the same pinned batches writes zero rows (the guard covers every value column and the batch provenance, not loaded_at). Plan facts are never retired or deleted (retract none): a batch that restates an application replaces its row, one that leaves the manifest leaves the row as the last stated values.

THREE write statements reach coa_notice_variances: the batched guarded upsert, the UNMARK UPDATE (keys back in the parse: retired_at -> NULL) and the MARK UPDATE (keys absent: retired_at = now(), first stamp kept) - the library departed_mark path. No DELETE exists. A run whose mass-retire guard suppresses the MARK traces 2 write fingerprints, so the witness capture must be a run the guard lets through. The derived coa_plan_facts upsert is derived_statements 1 (Spec 124 R-HA): issued once per run, with slice 0, only when a pinned batch carries plan facts.

on_prior_run_error_why.text: The prior completed run's coa_notices_load block carries the content_hash the skip compares against. A failed read must not degrade to 'first run' silently, and refusing is cheap because nothing has been fetched yet.

why.text: Migration 252 enables RLS on coa_notice_variances with ZERO policies (Spec 114 Class B). Under a non-bypass role the guarded upsert affects 0 rows with NO error, so the counters read 0 and the verdict reads PASS - indistinguishable from an unchanged manifest. The bypass is the precondition, checked before any document is fetched.

Migration 285 enables RLS on coa_plan_facts with ZERO policies (Spec 114 Class B). Under a non-bypass role the derived upsert affects 0 rows with NO error, so the plan facts would silently never load (Spec 124 R-CT).

batch_why.text: Generated (scripts/generate-ingest-batch.js, FLEET-2 B-3 #37): a step with two write targets declares "none" — the runner slices each target at its own write stride (pipeline.maxRowsPerInsert, Spec 124 R-CU), and the derived coa_plan_facts rows are emitted once, with slice 0 of the primary (R-DY (a), RE-FREEZE #40).

on_row_error_why.text: A variance item the reconcile drops (a superseded or same-date-conflicting duplicate notice) is a counted shaped_skipped reason, never a silent loss; per-document failures are closed doc_status values that FAIL the pre_write checks before any write.

on_check_error_why.text: Every check reads a count the arm or the reconcile already measured (acquired.document_set / acquired.reconcile); a check that throws is a defect in this step, so it must redden the run.

expect.violation_when: a fetched document hashes differently from its pinned manifest sha256

order_guarantee.guarantee: A document whose bytes changed since the pin must stop the run before any write: its parse would silently replace the pinned oracle. A re-pin is a reviewed manifest commit.
order_guarantee.anchor: no upsert and no MARK from a bad parse or an incomplete acquisition

why.text: C1 (Spec 129 §10). The arm hashes every document in memory and compares the pinned sha256; a mismatch is a doc_status, never a silent re-pin.

expect.violation_when: a document ended http_error, timeout, too_large, extract_error or no_text_layer

order_guarantee.guarantee: A document that could not be acquired or extracted must stop the run before any write: its rows would otherwise be soft-retired by the MARK.
order_guarantee.anchor: no upsert and no MARK from a bad parse or an incomplete acquisition

why.text: C2 (Spec 129 §10). Not a rate: a single skipped document would retire that notice set, so the fix is moving a dead document to excluded[] by commit.

expect.of: pair items over items citing By-law 569-2013

order_guarantee.guarantee: An extractor regression (pair rate under the pre-registered bound) must not upsert or retire anything.
order_guarantee.anchor: no upsert and no MARK from a bad parse or an incomplete acquisition

why.text: C3, pre-registered (Spec 129 §10): PASS >= 0.85 (the spike CI lower bound), WARN >= 0.80 with skip_write, FAIL below; a null rate (no 569 items) is unevaluable and reads FAIL. A first-run WARN is resolved only by extractor work under a new logic_version, never by editing the bound. LCN-D4 RULED 2026-10-07 (operator: fix the parser, bounds unchanged): the compound-sentence parse of coa-extractor-2 measures 0.888 on the spike corpus, 0.606 before (§5).

expect.of: minor-variance notices with no REQUESTED VARIANCE(S) section, percent

order_guarantee.guarantee: A segmentation regression that loses variance sections must not retire the rows of the notices it lost.
order_guarantee.anchor: no upsert and no MARK from a bad parse or an incomplete acquisition

why.text: C4 (spike 3.7 %). Signature pages and consent-only blocks are excluded from the denominator.

expect.violation_when: decision_mailed_on minus the manifest hearing_date falls outside [0, coa_notices_mail_lag_max_days]

order_guarantee.guarantee: The hearing date comes from the document title, not the notice text; a title/date mismatch would misdate every law-at-hearing comparison, so it must stop the write.
order_guarantee.anchor: no upsert and no MARK from a bad parse or an incomplete acquisition

why.text: C7a. The bounds are PROVISIONAL (14 days, 0 violations, from the spike 4-8 day lag) until build-manifest --measure (P0.4) measures every pinned document; the seed is updated in a commit before the first run if P0.4 says so.

expect.violation_when: a by-status map does not sum to its independently tallied total (docs, notices, items x3)

order_guarantee.guarantee: A counting defect means some notice or item went unaccounted, so nothing may be written or retired.
order_guarantee.anchor: no upsert and no MARK from a bad parse or an incomplete acquisition

why.text: C9 - the same-loop counting check at doc, notice and item level.

expect.violation_when: a pair row is mapped to a target whose McBylaw unit family differs from its parsed unit

order_guarantee.guarantee: A target-map defect would put a value under the wrong rule for every consumer; it must stop the write.
order_guarantee.anchor: no upsert and no MARK from a bad parse or an incomplete acquisition

why.text: C13, scoped to pair rows (P0.3 measured 0 over the spike pairs; 27 mismatches sit on non-pair rows whose values are not claimed).

expect.violation_when: an item's pair is in one unit family but its keyword-mapped target is in another; it is stored as target_unit_mismatch (values not claimed) instead of a pair

order_guarantee.guarantee: An item whose unit family disagrees with its mapped target must stay visible on every run even when its values are not claimed.
order_guarantee.anchor: no upsert and no MARK from a bad parse or an incomplete acquisition

why.text: Operator ruling 2026-10-09 (Spec 129 §5, Path 2): such items are not claimed as pairs; this count keeps every one visible on every run (Spec 124 Rule 1). C13 stays FAIL viol <= 0 as the backstop for pairs.

expect.violation_when: a values-only batch was built under a target-map version other than the current one, so its stored targets may be stale

order_guarantee.guarantee: A batch built under an older target map must stay visible on every run; its stored targets are not silently remapped.
order_guarantee.anchor: no upsert and no MARK from a bad parse or an incomplete acquisition

why.text: Spec 129 §2b (CHAT-71.2): a values batch carries targets mapped at build time from text the pipeline never holds. Its target_map_version is compared with the current target-map.json every run; a mismatch is a rebuild from the intake drop, never a silent remap (core.7).

order_guarantee.guarantee: One document whose layout the extractor cannot read must not dilute into a passing aggregate and then be written.

why.text: C12 - target-aware plausibility of the required (law) side; sample variance keys ride in the row detail.

plausibility.sql: SELECT count(DISTINCT v.application_number)::int FROM coa_notice_variances v LEFT JOIN coa_applications a ON a.application_number = v.application_number WHERE v.retired_at IS NULL AND a.application_number IS NULL

why.text: P1 - the soft reference to coa_applications (no FK by design, Spec 129 §4): notices whose application number CKAN does not carry. 0 of 164 on the spike. Declared 2026-10-07 against the EMPTY table (value 0): the first real value comes from the first captured run.

plausibility.sql: SELECT count(DISTINCT v.application_number)::int FROM coa_notice_variances v JOIN coa_applications a ON a.application_number = v.application_number WHERE v.retired_at IS NULL AND (v.decision = 'refused') IS DISTINCT FROM (a.decision ILIKE '%refus%')

why.text: P2 - refused per the notice vs refused per CKAN (G4: 16 = 16 on the spike). Declared 2026-10-07 against the EMPTY table (value 0): the first real value comes from the first captured run.

plausibility.sql: SELECT count(DISTINCT v.application_number)::int FROM coa_notice_variances v JOIN coa_applications a ON a.application_number = v.application_number WHERE v.retired_at IS NULL AND abs(v.hearing_date - a.hearing_date::date) > 1

why.text: P3 - G11: CKAN hearing_date is +1 day for most notices (LCN-D3); more than 1 day is a wrong pin or a re-hearing. Declared 2026-10-07 against the EMPTY table (value 0): the first real value comes from the first captured run.

plausibility.sql: SELECT count(*)::int FROM (SELECT application_number, item_ordinal FROM coa_notice_variances WHERE retired_at IS NULL GROUP BY 1, 2 HAVING count(*) > 1) d

why.text: P4 - duplicate active items across source families, or left by a mass-guard-suppressed MARK (Known Failure Mode). Declared 2026-10-07 against the EMPTY table (value 0): the first real value comes from the first captured run.

deviations.from: plan D10 listing the emits as 17 separate typed keys

why.text: The INGESTOR runner reads its prior/skip block as records_meta[emits[0].key] (scripts/lib/step/index.js runIngestPhase emitsList(descriptor)[0]), and the content-hash skip compares the content_hash of that block (source-version.js validatorEqualityDecision). The 17 keys therefore live in ONE object emit, coa_notices_load (the ravine_load / centreline_load precedent), plus spec_version, content_hash, source_dataset_version and skipped_reason for the DS4 skip re-emit.

deviations.adjudicated_by: orchestrator, implementation of the authorized WF1 plan (library constraint, measured) [register: Spec 124 R-HS; V3 condition-9 rulings 2026-10-20]

limitations.what: Raw notice text lives in JS strings until garbage collection; the byte buffer is zero-filled but strings cannot be. No disk, log or column holds them (T-PII-4).
limitations.measured: scripts/lib/pdf-text.js and the arm open no file (T-ACQ-11 spies, T-PII-4 token scan)

limitations.what: The consent-item rule (k) recognises a B-file number inside a variance item; mixed-notice layouts were not in the spike sample, so the first run reports consent_items_skipped for review.

recovery.reset: TRUNCATE is never correct here - the table is an oracle re-derivable from the pinned manifest. Re-run with COA_NOTICES_FORCE_RELOAD=1, which bypasses the content-hash skip and rewrites through the same guarded upsert plus soft retire.

interrupted_why.text: Rule 12 truthful posture (Spec 129 §D9): no retract all / full_only target, so this is not a destructive full retraction. One step-scoped transaction holds the upsert, UNMARK and MARK; a kill rolls all three back, and retire is soft and library-guarded.

before_image_why.text: The before-image mechanism mirrors a retraction's scope predicate as a SELECT; this target declares scope none and a SOFT retire (retired_at stamps, no DELETE), so no destroyed state exists to capture.
